name: BioMassters
description:
Above Ground Biomass is an important variable as forests play a crucial role in mitigating climate change as they act as an efficient, natural and cost-effective carbon sink. Traditional field and airborne LiDAR measurements have been proven to provide reliable estimations of forest biomass. Nevertheless, the use of these techniques at a large scale can be challenging and expensive. Satellite data have been widely used as a valuable tool in estimating biomass on a global scale. However, the full potential of dense multi-modal satellite time series data, in combination with modern deep learning approaches, has yet to be fully explored. The aim of the "BioMassters" data challenge and benchmark dataset is to investigate the potential of multi-modal satellite data (Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 MSI) to estimate forest biomass at a large scale using the Finnish Forest Centre's open forest and nature airborne LiDAR data as a reference. 
The performance of the top three baseline models shows the potential of deep learning to produce accurate and higher-resolution biomass maps. Our benchmark dataset is publically available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/nascetti-a/BioMassters (doi:10.57967/hf/1009) and the implementation of the top three winning models are available at https://github.com/drivendataorg/the-biomassters.
evaluation_method: RMSE (root mean squared error) and R^2 (coefficient of determination) for continuous biomass estimation
reputation: Well-regarded community challenge (DrivenData-style) with public dataset and reproducible winning solutions; used in remote-sensing biomass estimation research.
notes: Reference data derived from airborne LiDAR over Finland (geographic specificity / domain shift risk); multi-modal satellite time-series are provided but coverage is region-limited; challenge metrics report continuous regression errors rather than classification accuracy.
